idiom.title: Get wind of something
idiom.glossZh: “得知或听到某事” 或 “风闻”。通常指秘密或非公开的信息被无意中听到或发现。
idiom.interpretationEn: This phrase originates from nautical terminology. In old times, sailors relied on the wind to gauge their surroundings; if they “got wind” of something, it meant they became aware of it. Nowadays, the expression refers to someone unintentionally hearing or discovering some news or a secret.
idiom.interpretationZh: 这个短语源自航海术语。在旧时，航海员依靠风向来判断周围的事物，如果他们 “得到了风”，说明他们有所察觉。现如今，这个表达用于指某人无意中听到了某些消息或秘密。

examples.en: If they get wind of our plans, the surprise will be ruined.
examples.zh: 如果他们风闻了我们的计划，惊喜就会被破坏。

examples.en: I got wind of a change in the company’s management.
examples.zh: 我听说公司管理层有变动。

examples.en: She got wind of the rumors about the merger before anyone else.
examples.zh: 她最先风闻了关于合并的谣言。

people.name: Jannie du Plessis
people.extract: Jan Nathaniel du Plessis is a former South African rugby union player, who played as a prop for Montpellier in the French Top 14 and the Lions in Super Rugby. He played for the Free State Cheetahs in the Currie Cup and the Cheetahs in Super Rugby until 2007, when he joined Durban-based side the Sharks, where he played until 2015. He won 70 caps for South Africa between 2007 and 2015.
highlights: Former South African rugby union player.
Played as a prop for Montpellier and Lions.

people.name: Choudhry Rahmat Ali
people.extract: Chaudhary Rahmat Ali was a Muslim nationalist activist who is credited with coining the name "Pakistan" for a separate Muslim homeland in British India and is sometimes regarded as the originator of the Pakistan Movement.
highlights: Regarded as originator of Pakistan Movement.
